nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be the morphism on binary words with $\mu(0) = 01$ and $\mu(1) = 10$. If $w$ is a nonempty binary word of length $|w|$ with $\alpha$ alternations (positions where two adjacent letters differ), then $\mu(w)$ has exactly $2|w| - 1 - \alpha$ alternations.
nodes.title: Alternations of the Thue–Morse image of a word

nodes.summary: The number of alternations of a binary word $w$ is the number of occurrences of the factors $01$ and $10$ in $w$, that is, the number of positions $i$ with $w_i \ne w_{i+1}$.
nodes.title: Alternations of a binary word

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $M_n$ is the largest number of alternations (positions where two adjacent letters differ) among the length-$n$ factors of the Thue–Morse sequence.
nodes.title: Maximum number of alternations in Thue–Morse factors

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, let $m_k$ and $M_k$ be the least and the largest number of alternations (positions where two adjacent letters differ) among the length-$k$ factors of the Thue–Morse sequence. Then for every $n \ge 1$, $m_{4n} = 2n - 1 + m_{n+1}$, $M_{4n} = 2n + M_{n+1}$, $m_{4n+2} = 2n + m_{n+1}$ and $M_{4n+2} = 2n + 1 + M_{n+1}$.
nodes.title: Quadrupling recurrences for Thue–Morse alternation extrema

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, let $m_k$ and $M_k$ be the least and the largest number of alternations (positions where two adjacent letters differ) among the length-$k$ factors of the Thue–Morse sequence. Then for every $n \ge 2$, $m_{2n} = 2n - 1 - M_{n+1}$, $M_{2n} = 2n - 1 - m_n$, $m_{2n+1} = 2n - M_{n+1}$ and $M_{2n+1} = 2n - m_{n+1}$.
nodes.title: Doubling recurrences for Thue–Morse alternation extrema

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $m_n$ is the least number of alternations (positions where two adjacent letters differ) among the length-$n$ factors of the Thue–Morse sequence.
nodes.title: Minimum number of alternations in Thue–Morse factors

nodes.summary: The morphism $\mu$ sends each letter to a word of length two, $\mu(0) = 01$ and $\mu(1) = 10$, and a binary word $w_1 w_2 \cdots w_k$ to the concatenation $\mu(w_1) \mu(w_2) \cdots \mu(w_k)$.
nodes.title: Extension of the Thue–Morse substitution to binary words

nodes.summary: The regular paperfolding sequence $f = f_0 f_1 f_2 \cdots$ over $\{0, 1\}$ is indexed from $0$: for each $i$, write $i + 1 = m \cdot 2^k$ with $m$ odd; then $f_i = 0$ if $m \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ and $f_i = 1$ if $m \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.
nodes.title: Regular paperfolding sequence

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $w = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a binary word of length $2n + 1$ with $w_{2i} \ne w_{2i+2}$ for every $i < n$, so that its even positions read $abab\cdots$ with $a \ne b$ and its odd positions are arbitrary. Then the reduction of $w$, the word obtained by collapsing each maximal run of equal letters of $w$ to a single letter, has length $n + 1$; that is, $w$ has exactly $n + 1$…
nodes.title: Runs in a word whose even-position letters alternate

nodes.summary: The reduction $\operatorname{red}(w)$ of a binary word $w$ is the word obtained by collapsing each maximal run of equal consecutive letters of $w$ to a single letter; for example $\operatorname{red}(0011101) = 0101$.
nodes.title: Reduction of a binary word

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{ab,red}}_f(n)$ be the number of reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$, counted up to rearrangement of their letters. For every even $n > 0$, $\rho^{\mathrm{ab,red}}_f(n) = 3$.
nodes.title: Reduced abelian complexity of the paperfolding word at even lengths

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{ab,red}}_f(n)$ be the number of reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$, counted up to rearrangement of their letters. For every $n > 1$ with $n \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, $\rho^{\mathrm{ab,red}}_f(n) = 4$.
nodes.title: Reduced abelian complexity of the paperfolding word at lengths 1 mod 4

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{ab,red}}_f(n)$ be the number of reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$, counted up to rearrangement of their letters. For every natural number $n \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, $\rho^{\mathrm{ab,red}}_f(n) = 5$.
nodes.title: Reduced abelian complexity of the paperfolding word at lengths 3 mod 4

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n)$ be the number of distinct reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$. For every natural number $n$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(8n+5) = 6$.
nodes.title: Reduced complexity of the paperfolding word at lengths 8n + 5

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n)$ be the number of distinct reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$. For every $n \ge 1$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(8n+1) = 4$.
nodes.title: Reduced complexity of the paperfolding word at lengths 8n + 1

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n)$ be the number of distinct reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$. For every natural number $n$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(8n+7) = 6$.

nodes.title: Reduced complexity of the paperfolding word at lengths 8n + 3

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n)$ be the number of distinct reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$. For every $n \ge 2$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n) = 4$ if $n \equiv 0, 1, 2, 4$ or $6 \pmod 8$, and $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n) = 6$ if $n \equiv 3, 5$ or $7 \pmod 8$.
nodes.title: Reduced complexity of the paperfolding word

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n)$ be the number of distinct reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$. For every $n \ge 1$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(2n) = 4$.
nodes.title: Reduced complexity of the paperfolding word at even lengths

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be the Thue–Morse sequence and $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t$ its reduced factor complexity. For every natural number $m \ge 1$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t(4m) = \rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t(m+1) + 2$, and for every natural number $m \ge 0$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t(4m+2) = \rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t(m+1) + 2$.
nodes.title: Reduced complexity of the Thue–Morse word at even lengths

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be the Thue–Morse sequence and $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t$ its reduced factor complexity. For every odd natural number $n$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t(n) = \rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t((n+1)/2)$.
nodes.title: Reduced complexity of the Thue–Morse word at odd lengths

nodes.summary: For a finite binary word $w$, let $\mathrm{red}(w)$ be the word obtained from $w$ by collapsing each run of equal letters to a single letter. For an infinite binary word $x = x_0 x_1 x_2 \cdots$ and a natural number $n$, the reduced factor complexity $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_x(n)$ is the number of distinct words $\mathrm{red}(w)$ as $w$ ranges over the length-$n$ factors of $x$.

can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
